questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Five people P, Q, R, S and T work in a bank. P and Q don't like each other but have to share an office till T gets a promotion and moves to the big office next to the garden. R, who is currently sharing an office with T wants to move to the adjacent office with S, the handsome new intern. Given the floor plan, what is the current location of Q, R and T? (\(\text{O} = \text{Office}\), \(\text{WR} = \text{Washroom}\))
questions.explanation:
Constraints extracted from the problem:
  1. P and Q must share one office (forced by management until T gets promoted).
  2. T wants to move to the office adjacent to S's office.
  3. R currently shares with T and wants to move to the adjacent office with S.
  4. After T moves next to garden (big office), R and S share an office.
Evaluating options:
  • (a) P alone in O1, Q alone in O2 — P and Q not sharing; violates constraint 1.
  • (b) P,Q in O1; T in O3; R,S in O4 — R and T are not adjacent to S; violates the adjacency requirement.
  • (c) P,Q in O1; R,T in O3; S in O4 — P and Q share (); R and T share, with S in the adjacent office (); layout consistent with all constraints. \(\checkmark\)
  • (d) P,Q in O1; R in O3; S in O4; T in Manager's room — T moving to manager's room is not described; inconsistent.
\[\boxed{\text{(C)}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The missing number in the given sequence 343, 1331, ____, 4913 is
questions.explanation:
Identify the pattern in the series \(343,\;1331,\;\_\_,\;4913\): \[343  = 7^{3}, \qquad
    1331 = 11^{3}, \qquad
    4913 = 17^{3}\] The bases are consecutive prime numbers: \(7,\;11,\;13,\;17,\;\ldots\) Missing term corresponds to the prime \(13\): \[13^{3} = 2197\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 2197}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: How many integers are there between 100 and 1000 all of whose digits are even?
questions.explanation:
We need 3-digit integers (100 to 999) where every digit is even. Even digits available: \(\{0,\;2,\;4,\;6,\;8\}\) — five choices.
  • Hundreds digit: cannot be 0 (else the number \(< 100\)). Choices: \(\{2,\;4,\;6,\;8\}\) \(= 4\) options.
  • Tens digit: any even digit including 0. Choices: \(\{0,\;2,\;4,\;6,\;8\}\) \(= 5\) options.
  • Units digit: any even digit including 0. Choices: \(\{0,\;2,\;4,\;6,\;8\}\) \(= 5\) options.
\[\text{Total} = 4 \times 5 \times 5 = 100\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 100}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The ratio of the number of boys and girls who participated in an examination is 4:3. The total percentage of candidates who passed the examination is 80 and the percentage of girls who passed is 90. The percentage of boys who passed is ______.
questions.explanation:
Let number of boys \(= 4x\) and number of girls \(= 3x\), so total students \(= 7x\). Total students who passed (80% of total): \[\frac{80}{100} \times 7x = 5.6x\] Girls who passed (90% of girls): \[\frac{90}{100} \times 3x = 2.7x\] Boys who passed:
\[5.6x - 2.7x = 2.9x\] Percentage of boys who passed (out of total boys \(= 4x\)): \[\frac{2.9x}{4x} \times 100 = \frac{2.9}{4} \times 100 = 72.50\,\%\] \[\boxed{\text{B) 72.50}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Given two sets \(X = \{1, 2, 3\}\) and \(Y = \{2, 3, 4\}\), we construct a set Z of all possible fractions where the numerators belong to set X and the denominators belong to set Y. The product of elements having minimum and maximum values in the set Z is ______.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: On a horizontal ground, the base of a straight ladder is 6 m away from the base of a vertical pole. The ladder makes an angle of 45 to the horizontal. If the ladder is resting at a point located at one-fifth of the height of the pole from the bottom, the height of the pole is ____ meters.
questions.explanation:
The ladder makes \(45^{\circ}\) with the horizontal ground. The base of the ladder is \(6\,\text{m}\) from the pole. The ladder rests at a point that is \(\tfrac{1}{5}\) of the pole's height \(H\) from the bottom. \[\tan 45^{\circ} = 1\] The ladder meets the pole at height \(\dfrac{H}{5}\), and the horizontal distance is \(6\,\text{m}\): \[\tan 45^{\circ} = \frac{H/5}{6} = 1\] \[\frac{H}{5} = 6 \implies H = 30\,\text{m}\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 30}}\]
Key points
  • \(\tan\theta = \dfrac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}\); the opposite side here is the height at which the ladder rests (\(H/5\)), not the full pole height \(H\).
  • \(\tan 45^{\circ} = 1\), so opposite \(=\) adjacent \(\implies \dfrac{H}{5} = 6 \implies H = 30\,\text{m}\).

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: If E = 10; J = 20; O = 30; and T = 40, what will be P + E + S + T?
questions.explanation: Each letter is assigned its positional value in the alphabet. Using the given key: \(E=10,\;J=20,\;O=30,\;T=40\), the pattern is that each letter's value equals its position multiplied by a constant. Decoding the remaining letters: \[P = 32,\quad E = 10,\quad S = 38,\quad T = 40\] \[P + E + S + T = 32 + 10 + 38 + 40 = 120\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 120}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The new cotton technology, Bollgard-II, with herbicide tolerant traits has developed into a thriving business in India. However, the commercial use of this technology is not legal in India. Notwithstanding that, reports indicate that the herbicide tolerant Bt cotton had been purchased by farmers at an average of Rs 200 more than the control price of ordinary cotton, and planted in 15% of the cotton growing area in the 2017 Kharif season. Which one of the following statements can be inferred from the given passage?
options: Farmers want to access the new technology if India benefits from it
Farmers want to access the new technology even if it is not legal
Farmers want to access the new technology for experimental purposes
Farmers want to access the new technology by paying high price
questions.explanation:
The passage states that despite the commercial use of Bollgard-II being illegal in India, farmers purchased it in significant quantities (15% of the cotton-growing area in the 2017 Kharif season), paying a premium of Rs,200 more than control-price cotton.
  • (a) Only if India benefits — the passage shows farmers acted regardless of national policy benefit.
  • (b) Even if not legal — the passage emphasises widespread adoption despite illegality; farmers paid extra to access the technology illegally. \(\checkmark\)
  • (c) Experimental purposes — the scale of adoption (15% of area) suggests commercial, not experimental, use.
  • (d) By paying high price — partial truth; price detail is secondary to the core inference about illegality.
\[\boxed{\text{B) Farmers want to access the new technology even if it is not legal}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: In a sports academy of 300 people, 105 play only cricket, 70 play only hockey, 50 play only football, 25 play both cricket and hockey, 15 play both hockey and football and 30 play both cricket and football. The rest of them play all three sports. What is the percentage of people who play at least two sports?
questions.explanation:
Given data for 300 people in a sports academy: \[\text{Only Cricket} = 105,\quad \text{Only Hockey} = 70,\quad \text{Only Football} = 50\] \[\text{Cricket} \cap \text{Hockey only} = 25,\quad \text{Hockey} \cap \text{Football only} = 15,\quad \text{Cricket} \cap \text{Football only} = 30\] Total accounted for in exactly-one and exactly-two categories: \[105 + 70 + 50 + 25 + 15 + 30 = 295\] Players in all three sports: \[300 - 295 = 5\] Players playing at least 2 sports (exactly two \(+\) all three): \[25 + 30 + 15 + 5 = 75\] Percentage: \[\frac{75}{300} \times 100 = 25\,\%\] \[\boxed{\text{B) 25.00}}\]
Key points
  • ``At least 2 sports'' \(=\) (exactly 2 sports) \(+\) (all 3 sports).
  • Find the all-three region by subtracting the sum of all other exclusive regions from the total.
Mistakes to avoid
  • The pairwise intersection values given (25, 15, 30) are exclusive pairwise regions (not including the all-three overlap); do not subtract the all-three count again.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: A square has sides 5 cm smaller than the sides of a second square. The area of the larger square is four times the area of the smaller square. The side of the larger square is ___ cm.
questions.explanation:
Let the side of the larger square \(= x\,\text{cm}\). \[\text{Side of smaller square} = (x - 5)\,\text{cm}\] \[\text{Area of larger square} = x^{2}, \qquad \text{Area of smaller square} = (x-5)^{2}\] Given condition — area of larger square is four times that of smaller: \[x^{2} = 4(x-5)^{2}\] \[x^{2} = 4(x^{2} - 10x + 25)\] \[x^{2} = 4x^{2} - 40x + 100\] \[3x^{2} - 40x + 100 = 0\] Taking the positive square root of both sides of \(x = 2(x-5)\) (since \(x > 0\) and \(x > 5\)): \[x = 2(x - 5) \implies x = 2x - 10 \implies x = 10\,\text{cm}\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 10.00}}\]
Key points
  • \(x^{2} = 4(x-5)^{2}\) implies \(x = \pm\,2(x-5)\); take the positive root that satisfies \(x > 5\).
  • Verify: larger area \(= 100\), smaller area \(= 25\); \(100 = 4 \times 25\). \(\checkmark\)

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Daytime temperatures in Delhi can ______ 40 C.
questions.explanation:
The sentence requires a verb that collocates naturally with a temperature value to indicate that temperatures attain a particular level.
  • (a) get — informal; ``get 40°C'' is non-standard.
  • (b) stand — used for static readings (``the temperature stands at''), not for attaining a maximum.
  • (c) reach — standard collocation: ``temperatures can reach 40°C'' is idiomatic and correct. \(\checkmark\)
  • (d) peak — intransitive; cannot be followed directly by a temperature value without a preposition.
\[\boxed{\text{C) reach}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: The growth rate of ABC Motors in 2017 was the same _____ XYZ Motors in 2016.
questions.explanation:
The sentence compares ``the growth rate of ABC Motors'' (singular noun phrase) with ``the growth rate of XYZ Motors''. The correct comparative structure requires a singular demonstrative pronoun ``that of'' to avoid repeating the noun phrase.
  • (a) as off — ungrammatical.
  • (b) as those of — ``those'' is plural; the subject
  • (c) as that off — ``off'' is incorrect (should be ``of''). (growth rate) is singular.
  • (d) as that of — ``that'' correctly substitutes the singular noun ``growth rate''; ``of'' completes the possessive. \(\checkmark\)
\[\boxed{\text{D) as that of}}\]

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: Suresh wanted to lay a new carpet in his new mansion with an area of \(70 \times 55\) sq. mts. However an area of 550 sq. mts. had to be left out for flower pots. If the cost of carpet is Rs. 50 per sq. mts., how much money (in Rs.) will be spent by Suresh for the carpet now?
questions.explanation:
Total area of the mansion: \[70 \times 55 = 3850\,\text{sq.\,m}\] Area to be carpeted (subtracting flower-pot area): \[3850 - 550 = 3300\,\text{sq.\,m}\] Cost of carpet at Rs.,50 per sq.,m: \[3300 \times 50 = \text{Rs.}\;1{,}65{,}000\] \[\boxed{\text{A) Rs.\;1{,}65{,}000}}\]
Key points
  • Net carpeted area \(=\) Total area \(-\) Area left out.
  • Cost \(=\) Net area \(\times\) Rate per unit area.

questions.subject: general-aptitude
questions.question: A retaining wall with measurements \(30\,\text{m} \times 12\,\text{m} \times 6\,\text{m}\) was constructed with bricks of dimensions \(8\,\text{cm} \times 6\,\text{cm} \times 6\,\text{cm}\). If 60% of the wall consists of bricks, the number of bricks used for the construction is ____ lakhs.
questions.explanation:
Wall dimensions: \(30\,\text{m} \times 12\,\text{m} \times 6\,\text{m}\). Brick dimensions: \(8\,\text{cm} \times 6\,\text{cm} \times 6\,\text{cm}\). Bricks constitute \(60\%\) of the wall volume. Converting wall dimensions to cm and equating volumes: \[30 \times 12 \times 6 \times 10^{6}\,\text{cm}^{3} \times 0.6 = 8 \times 6 \times 6\,\text{cm}^{3} \times x\] \[x = \frac{30 \times 12 \times 6 \times 10^{6} \times 0.6}{8 \times 6 \times 6}\] \[x = 4.5 \times 10^{6} = 45 \times 10^{5} = 45\,\text{lakh bricks}\] \[\boxed{\text{C) 45}}\]
Key points
  • Convert all dimensions to the same unit before equating volumes.
  • Number of bricks \(= \dfrac{\text{Wall volume} \times \text{brick fraction}}{\text{Volume of one brick}}\).

questions.question: Mohan, the manager, wants his four workers to work in pairs. No pair should work for more than 5 hours. Ram and John have worked together for 5 hours. Krishna and Amir have worked as a team for 2 hours. Krishna does not want to work with Ram. Whom should Mohan allot to work with John, if he wants all the workers to continue working?
questions.explanation:
Constraints:
  • Ram and John have already worked together for 5 hours — their pair is complete (max 5 hours reached).
  • Krishna and Amir have worked together for 2 hours — 3 hours remain.
  • Krishna cannot work with Ram.
  • All four workers must continue working.
Since Ram--John are done and Krishna--Ram is forbidden, The new pairs must be formed from \(\{\text{John, Krishna, Ram, Amir}\}\): \[\text{New Pair 1: John and Krishna} \qquad \text{New Pair 2: Ram and Amir}\] John should be allotted to work with Krishna. \[\boxed{\text{B) Krishna}}\]
